source.title: Non-linear Interventions on Large Language Models

page_placements.theme: Directions and maps other than DIM also control refusal; DIM is not the unique or optimal handle

record.tranche_reason: The study runs DIM ablation, the difference-in-means refusal-direction baseline, on new instruct models and reports harmful-prompt refusal-bypass scores. It also compares linear and non-linear interventions.
record.gate_note: The study reports the DIM ablation scores only in Figure 1, without numerical values; they are recorded as figure-only. Intervention magnitudes in Table 1 are not rows because they measure edit size, not refusal behavior. The paper's loss-site selection statistics are not reported as intervention outcomes. RDO results and DIM ActAdd are not included as version-linked rows: the former is not the specified difference-in-means direction, and the reported measure uses harmful prompts rather than measuring refusal on harmless prompts as V1's addition claim requires.
record.test_reason: DIM ablation (Arditi et al.) appears only as a baseline for the authors' non-linear intervention. Its StrongREJECT scores on Llama3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct are shown only in Figure 1. The text says only that the non-linear method reaches scores 'comparable to the baselines'. The paper reports no number for DIM, no harmless-prompt addition test and no capability check. Its analyses (Tables 2–3, Figure 2) concern the authors' own method and its linear ablations, not the single DIM direction. So it uses the finding as a comparator rather than testing it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right, but overstated. The authors say the non-linear intervention reaches StrongREJECT scores comparable to, not better than, the linear baselines (DIM, RDO). It does so while editing one site with an edit norm more than two orders of magnitude smaller. They argue this reflects a non-linear feature governing refusal, located mainly in middle layers.
record.recipe_differences: The DIM baseline is described as extracting a class-mean refusal direction and ablating it at every token and module output, matching the claimed intervention. The study uses Llama3-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, its own prompt sets, and StrongREJECT evaluation.
record.method_sensitivity: The non-linear intervention's effectiveness varies with intervention layer: it is largely ineffective early, peaks in middle layers, and declines later (Section 5.3; Figure 2).

fits_no_version.finding: A learned invertible non-linear map (i-ResNet, k=1), clamped at one site, bypasses refusal: StrongREJECT 0.813 on Llama3-8B and 0.760 on Qwen2.5-7B. Edit norm is over 100x smaller than DIM ablation. Constraining the map to be linear drops scores to 0.010 and 0.072. Effectiveness peaks at middle layers.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Refusal can be controlled through a non-linear feature, located mainly in middle layers, more economically than through linear refusal directions.

record.problems: The Figure 1 DIM ablation values are not stated numerically, and the study does not evaluate general capability preservation. The comparison with non-linear steering is not itself a direct test of whether the DIM direction alone mediates refusal.
record.rows_left_out: No additional claim-linked results were left out. Table 1 edit magnitudes were omitted because they measure intervention size, not refusal behavior. RDO comparisons and DIM ActAdd were omitted because the former is not the specified difference-in-means direction and the latter's harmful-prompt measure does not test refusal on harmless prompts.

untested.parts: Inducing refusal by adding the direction on harmless prompts, preservation of other capabilities, and reported numeric ablation effects.
All of it: no weight edit or released abliterated models.
All of it: no affine, cone or multi-direction test. The paper's non-linear feature claim is recorded under fits_no_version.

missing.what: Numeric StrongREJECT values for DIM ablation and DIM ActAdd versus no intervention. These are readable only from the plot.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V1 limits_scope label rests on r5 and r6, which are the authors' own per-site linear ablation rather than the single DIM direction, so it is removed. The only V1-relevant evidence (r2, r4) appears only in Figure 1 and is described only as comparable. Table 1 shows DIM ablation edits about 50k sites per sample, which is intervention size, not a refusal outcome. The RDO ActAdd result on Qwen (0.020) was excluded by the authors as unreliable.

versions.untested_parts: The paper does not test whether adding the direction causes refusal on harmless prompts, or whether other abilities remain intact after ablation.
No weight-edit or released-model abliteration experiment.
No jailbreak-suppression mechanism or training against ablation is tested.
The paper investigates a non-linear feature map but does not test whether refusal is represented by an affine structure, cone, or multiple refusal directions.
No separation of harmfulness judgment from refusal decision is tested.
No cross-language, base-to-instruct, or model-variant transfer test.
No comparison of refusal training methods or training stages.

relation.reason: Uses DIM as a comparator and class-mean directions as a training tool. Reports no number of its own on whether DIM ablation removes refusal.

tranche.reason: DIM ablation is only a baseline, with StrongREJECT scores shown only in Figure 1 and no numbers in the text. The method's loss uses class-mean-difference directions as supervision. The rows report only the authors' method and its own variants. The study does not argue that the DIM direction fails or that a version is wrong.

source_check.notes: Figure 1 has DIM ablation/ActAdd StrongREJECT scores on Llama3-8B and Qwen2.5-7B (figure only; a figure reading could add a V1 replication on Qwen). Footnote: RDO ActAdd on Qwen scored 0.020 and was excluded as unreliable. There is no capability measure. Within the record, r7/r8 keep 'observed' while r9/r10 were set to cannot_determine because unlinked rows have no state meaning, which is inconsistent.

statements.correction: i-ResNet f_theta, k=1, clamped to the cached harmless mean at one site (Llama layer 10 pos -3; Qwen layer 14 pos -4). StrongREJECT on 313 prompts: 0.813 Llama3-8B-Instruct, 0.760 Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct. Edit L2: 3.5 vs DIM ablation 2,898.7 (Llama); 28.3 vs 41,376.2 (Qwen). Linear-constrained f_theta: 0.010 Llama, 0.072 Qwen (Table 3).
statements.problem: 'Constraining the map to be linear drops the score to 0.010' gives the Llama value only, though the sentence reads as covering both models. On Qwen the linear-constrained map scores 0.072. The other numbers are right: 0.813, 0.760, and an edit norm over 100x below DIM ablation.
